A weak wind flow from the southwest will dominate the city, contributing to the persistence of the humid conditions. Residents in low-lying areas such as Gwarinpa and parts of Maitama can expect the heat index to be even more pronounced, making the outside environment feel particularly uncomfortable. The UV index will be moderate, ranging from 4 to 6, which is not unusual for this time of year. As the day progresses, there is a 70 percent chance of rainfall, with the most likely time for precipitation being in the late afternoon or early evening. The precipitation is expected to be intense but brief, with accumulation ranges varying between 10 and 30 millimeters.
The rainfall accumulation will be influenced by the strength of the low-pressure system and the moisture content in the atmosphere. Models suggest that the system will strengthen throughout the day, leading to an increased chance of downpours in the evening. However, the exact timing and intensity of the rainfall are still uncertain, and my best guess is that the precipitation will be most intense in areas with higher elevation, such as Aso Rock and the surrounding hills. The wind direction will shift from southwest to northwest in the evening, which may lead to a slight decrease in temperature and humidity levels. The evening commute may be affected by the rainfall, particularly on roads such as the airport road and the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. The traffic is currently light, but the situation may change rapidly if the rainfall becomes heavy. Residents are advised to check the latest traffic updates before embarking on their journey home.
